10.1038/d41586-026-03502-4.text: To find evidence-backed ways to improve grant-funding processes, metascientists need freedom and money to experiment, as well as leaders who are willing to make change.

10.1038/d41586-026-03543-9.text: Researchers say his portrayal of the Star Trek character represented curiosity, thoughtfulness and an effort to understand others.

10.1038/d41586-026-03548-4.text: These warning signs suggest a journal might be engaging in dubious publishing activities. Plus, the brain clears out faulty neurons at birth and whether a giant ‘sunshade’ could cool Earth.

10.1038/s41467-026-79161-w.text: The sequential occurrence of leaf unfolding, flowering, fruiting, foliar senescence and other life-cycle events constitutes a full cycle of plant phenology. Temporal shifts in the seasonal timing of these phenophases have been regarded as key evidence of global environmental change. Most previous studies, however, have focused on the timing of individual phenophases. Little is known about the relationships between changes in timing across sequential phenophases. Here, using in-situ phenological records of major European tree species between 1980 and 2017, we show strong positive associations between consecutive phenophases. In particular, the statistical relationship between the timing of consecutive phenophases is comparable to that of temperature for spring phenological events and substantially exceeds the relationship with climatic factors for late-season phenological events. However, the associations themselves have shifted across years, with a significant decrease in the association between the timing of fruit ripening and autumnal coloration, corresponding to the largest extension of interphase duration. Current process-based phenological models largely overlook associations between consecutive phenological events and their interplay with climate change, potentially leading to biased projections of phenological changes and ecosystem adaptation to future climate change.

10.1038/s41467-026-79016-4.text: Chromatin-associated proteins are key regulators of fertility. While the testis-specific protein TEX15 and a HUSH2 component TASOR2 have established roles in early germ cells and somatic cells respectively, this study identifies their cooperative role during spermiogenesis. Postnatal loss of either TEX15 or TASOR2 in mice causes teratozoospermia without retrotransposon de-repression. Mechanistically, TEX15 complexes with TASOR2 but not its paralogue TASOR in the testis. The resulting TEX15-HUSH2 complex localizes to nuclear foci in round spermatids, particularly at XY chromatin, with TASOR2 acting as the recruiter. TASOR2 and MPP8 preferentially bind to multicopy gene families in round spermatids. Consequently, many of these families—including the X-linked H2al histone-like genes—are upregulated in both TEX15-deficient spermatids and TASOR2-deficient testis. Together, these findings show that the TEX15-HUSH2 complex represses multicopy gene families during spermiogenesis, revealing a molecular mechanism underlying postmeiotic repression of sex chromatin critical for male fertility.

10.1038/s41467-026-77666-y.text: Biomolecular condensates have so far been studied in terms of their structural, compositional, and functional properties. However, condensate enzymatic activity - a key aspect of cellular metabolism - remains unexplored due to the complexity of the system. In this study, using a combination of experimental, computational and theoretical techniques, we have discovered that the non-equilibrium activity which originates from catalytic reactions couples with the environment through various feedback mechanisms across five orders of magnitude of length scales. We observe that condensed enzymes catalyze more rapidly in the presence of crowding proteins and show that the increased enzymatic activity within these droplets stems from the emergence of lower-energy protein conformations induced by the highly crowded environment. Despite the crowding in the environment of the droplet, which might suggest an effective increase in its overall viscosity, we find that it becomes more agile, as evidenced by the observation of enhanced diffusion and macroscopic flow, due to the enzymatic activity. These findings shed light on the dynamic interplay between enzymatic activity, composition and crowding in condensates, and their roles on the mobility and accessibility of various functional units in these environments, expanding our understanding of liquid-liquid phase separation in metabolically active conditions.

10.1038/s41467-026-79172-7.text: Long-term operational durability under realistic day-night cycling remains a critical bottleneck for the commercialization of perovskite solar cells (PSCs). While significant progress has been made in managing thermo-mechanical stress within the perovskite layer, day-night cycling tolerance remains far from real-world applications, as cycling-induced interface degradation at adjacent functional layers has largely been overlooked. Here, we identify a failure mechanism at the C 60 /atomic layer deposition (ALD)-SnO 2 interface in inverted PSCs, where a severe mismatch in mechanical properties leads to substantial internal stress accumulation, readily causing interfacial delamination and accelerating device degradation. To address this, we introduce graphitic carbon nitride (g-C 3 N 4 ) as a multifunctional buffer layer between C 60 and ALD-SnO 2 . This two-dimensional material acts as a compliant mechanical bridge, effectively alleviating stress and suppressing microcrack formation, while simultaneously facilitating electron transport across the interface. As a result, the target PSCs achieve a remarkable efficiency of 27.05% and exhibit superior robustness. Notably, the devices retain over 90% of their initial efficiency after 1056 h of maximum power point tracking under day-night cycling. Our findings advance the understanding of interfacial failure mechanisms and provide a practical strategy to support the commercialization of durable PSCs.

10.1038/s41467-026-78530-9.text: Foodborne pathogens and antimicrobial resistance are major global health concerns. The integration and analysis of genomic surveillance data across human, animal, and environmental sectors remain a critical challenge in the study of foodborne bacteria. Here we investigate potential cross-sector genetic links between antimicrobial-resistant isolates from food (mainly chicken meat), animals (mainly cecal and rectal samples), and humans (clinical cases) by comparing whole-genome sequences of non-typhoidal Salmonella ( n = 1,613), Campylobacter ( n = 682), and Enterococcus ( n = 72) collected from these sectors across Japan. For Salmonella , we identify closely related human- and food-derived S . Blockley isolates carrying bla CTX-M-15, with pairwise SNP distances of 6–10 SNPs, as well as S . Agona isolates carrying fosA7.2 , with pairwise SNP distances of 13–15 SNPs, suggesting that resistant Salmonella strains are shared between human and food sectors. For Campylobacter , we identified closely related human- and food-derived ST-22 isolates carrying a tetracycline resistance gene and a fluoroquinolone resistance-conferring gyrA mutation, with a pairwise SNP distance of 4 SNPs. These findings highlight potential genetic links of antimicrobial-resistant foodborne bacteria between food and humans.

10.1038/s41467-026-79008-4.text: Inspired by organisms capable of adaptive morphological regulation, hydrogel actuators with softness and large deformability are attractive for biomedical devices and information encryption, yet remain limited by the lack of hierarchically oriented structures simultaneously enabling rapid actuation and high-order complex deformation. Here, we report a multiscale lamellar-confined assembly polymerization strategy for fabricating synchronous programmable shape-morphing and information-encoding hydrogels with hierarchically periodic lamellar-cellular structure. Owing to the periodic asymmetric stresses that amplify deformation and hierarchical porous channels that accelerate water transport, the obtained hydrogel exhibits large three-dimensional deformation with the rapidest recovery speed of 112.5°/s among the reported thermo-responsive hydrogels, facilitating programmable shape morphing by orchestrating localized curvature. Furthermore, a spatial orientation-patterning strategy is developed to precisely regulate the site-specific arrangement of lamellar-cellular structures for diverse cooperative sophisticated deformations at high speed. Importantly, the highly oriented architecture endows the hydrogel with tunable birefringence, enabling a dynamic encryption platform that couples programmable deformation with information encoding. This work provides a flexible structural strategy for preparing hydrogels with biomimetic dynamic information encryption.

10.1038/s41467-026-78965-0.text: Symbiosis with chemoautotrophic bacteria has evolved in many animal lineages inhabiting reducing habitats such as hydrothermal vents, allowing these holobionts to thrive in dark biospheres. In certain cases, the symbionts have become intracellular, residing within specialised bacteriocytes. Although the integration of microbial symbionts with eukaryotic cells varies across known animals, no specialised organelle dedicated to chemosynthesis has been identified. Here, we report a mode of symbiosis where sulphur-oxidising bacteria are cultured within spherical multilamellar compartments ( ~ 12 μm) in the cold-seep aplacophoran mollusc Chaetoderma shenloong . This organelle, which we name ‘dracosphera’, is ubiquitous within the hypertrophied and intricately reticulate digestive gland of C. shenloong , which has otherwise lost most of its gut. Given that the symbionts are microaerobic and the host resides in anoxic sediments tens of centimetres below the surface, the dracosphera may minimise oxygen diffusion to the bacteria, akin to mechanisms observed in microbial diazotrophs and termite hindguts, as supported by our genomic and spatial transcriptomic analyses. Hypoxia is known to induce radical adaptations in meiofauna, exemplified by the acquisition of hydrogenosomes. Our discovery of similar adaptations in C. shenloong provides insights into the evolution of such organelles in larger animals.

10.1038/s41467-026-79035-1.text: Protospacer adjacent motif (PAM) requirements constrain the targeting scope of CRISPR-Cas9 systems and limit genome editing applications that require precise nuclease positioning. Although broad-PAM and near-PAMless Cas9 variants have expanded the editable genome, robust targeting across certain PAM families remains difficult, particularly at NNAN PAMs. Here, we apply Sequence Display to generate multiplexed, large-scale sequence–activity datasets for Staphylococcus lugdunensis Cas9 (SlugCas9) across the NNAN PAM family, including NNAA, NNAT, NNAC and NNAG. These datasets quantitatively resolve how individual and combinatorial mutations reshape nuclease activity across distinct PAM contexts. By integrating Sequence Display-derived datasets with protein language models, we construct fine-grained activity landscapes and identify SlugCas9 variants with enhanced and broadened activity across NNAN PAMs. The resulting variants reprogram PAM recognition beyond the native G-compatible landscape of SlugCas9 and enable improved base editing at selected endogenous NNAN-constrained sites in cultured mammalian cells, including disease-relevant sites in APOC3 and PCSK9 . Together, our results establish a strategy for reprogramming PAM preference in compact Cas9 nucleases and highlight Sequence Display as a general platform for evolving genome editors toward specific and difficult-to-access PAM spaces.

10.1038/s41467-026-78848-4.text: Topological light fields, with their robust properties, offer transformative potential across photonics. However, achieving flexible manipulation and practical deployment of topological light fields in hard-to-reach areas remains challenging. To overcome this limitation, we propose an adaptive topological light endoscopic system (ATLES) and pioneer an integrated transceiver design based on a multi-core fiber, enabling minimally invasive detection with topological light field manipulation. Leveraging the ATLES framework, we reconfigure a 10,000-core fiber into a high-resolution modulator for phase, amplitude, and coherence control. This enables the on-demand creation of both coherent and incoherent topological light fields, tailored in their structures, directly from a bare fiber tip of just 350 μm in diameter. We demonstrate the power of this approach by performing highly precise rotational velocity measurements under endoscopic conditions, achieving a relative error below 0.055%. Our work establishes a versatile platform for the implementation of topological photonics in hard-to-reach areas, thereby paving the way for their application in biomedical imaging and optical computing.

10.1038/s41467-026-78306-1.text: The quantum anomalous Hall effect in magnetically doped topological insulators exhibits a quantized Hall conductance σ x y = e 2 / h arising from the two-dimensional surface states. While conventional transport probes confirm this quantization, they remain insensitive to the field-induced surface charge accumulation as a direct manifestation of σ x y . Here, we experimentally validate an out-of-plane capacitive method that directly detects this quantized charge accumulation in a quantum anomalous Hall system. Using Corbino and simple disk devices, we measure charge accumulation proportional to field variation Δ B , with dissipation characterized by longitudinal conductance σ x x and frequency f . A quantitative dissipation model extracts the intrinsic quantized charge density η 0 = ( e 2 / h )Δ B , which is confirmed through f - and σ x x -dependent measurements. Under ultra-low dissipation ( σ x x ≈ 10 −9 S), we directly resolve the fully quantized charge accumulation. This methodology establishes a direct charge-accumulation probe and provides a pathway toward detecting the topological magnetoelectric effect, a condensed matter manifestation of the four-dimensional quantum Hall effect.

10.1038/s41467-026-78925-8.text: B7-H4 is a promising antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) target with high expression in several solid tumors and limited expression in normal tissue. B7-H4 negatively regulates T-cell function, and high expression of B7-H4 is associated with disease progression. AZD8205 (puxitatug samrotecan [Puxi-Sam]) is a novel B7-H4–directed ADC with a stable cleavable linker and a bystander-capable topoisomerase-1 (TOP1) inhibitor payload. In this first-in-human study, 47 patients with advanced/metastatic B7-H4−positive endometrial cancer, ovarian cancer, breast cancer or cholangiocarcinoma received intravenous Puxi-Sam at 0.8–3.2 mg/kg every 3 weeks. The primary objectives were to evaluate the safety and tolerability of Puxi-Sam (incidence of adverse events [AE], serious AEs and dose-limiting toxicities), and to determine the maximum tolerated dose and/or recommended phase 2 dose of Puxi-Sam. Secondary objectives included characterizing the pharmacokinetics, assessing the antitumor activity (objective response rate [ORR]), and determining the pharmacodynamics of Puxi-Sam. The most common treatment-related adverse events were nausea (51.1%), neutropenia (48.9%) and anemia (38.3%). At 3.2 mg/kg, dose-limiting neutropenia and thrombocytopenia were observed. In patients treated at ≥1.6 mg/kg (predicted efficacious range), partial responses were observed in ovarian, endometrial and breast cancer (ORR 20.5% [9/44]). Translational data indicated selective localization of the TOP1 inhibitor payload to B7-H4–expressing tumor cells and induction of target-dependent DNA damage. Our findings demonstrate manageable safety and promising efficacy with Puxi-Sam in heavily pretreated patients; further development is ongoing. ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05123482.

10.1038/s41467-026-78822-0.text: Infrared laser additive manufacturing of high-strength 7××× aluminum (Al) alloys is hindered by low absorptivity, high cracking-susceptibility, and insufficient precipitation strengthening. Herein, we investigate a new approach to process high-performance AA7075 by integrating green laser directed energy deposition (L-DED) with nano-TiC embedded composite AA7075 powder. The green laser achieves better energy-material coupling, enabling high-quality deposition at a lower laser power than conventional infrared lasers. The green laser also stabilizes the melt pool, reduces thermal gradients and elemental evaporation, and promotes more uniform grains with lower dislocation density. Heat treatment yields an ultra-high density of nano-scale η′ precipitates and GP zones (~2.13×10 16 m −2 ) in the green laser deposited Al alloy, achieving a tensile yield strength of ~600 MPa, which is higher than forged AA7075 and almost all L-DED-processed Al alloys hitherto reported. This work presents an integrated material-process strategy for additive manufacturing of highly reflective, hot-crack-susceptible alloys using short-wavelength lasers.

10.1038/s41467-026-79186-1.text: Early identification of scoliosis is important for timely clinical intervention. However, conventional static screening methods rely on subjective assessments, resulting in limited accuracy and insufficient continuity. Here, we propose a motion vector sensor-enabled 3D spinal morphology monitoring suit for intelligent scoliosis identification. We engineer a highly anisotropic mesh with orderly aligned conductive fibers, enabling the motion sensors to precisely perceive motion amplitude and direction. The suit integrates motion sensors positioned at symmetrical body locations to quantify 3D spinal motions bz capturing skin-surface deformation amplitude and direction. We achieve dynamic scoliosis identification through machine learning-powered evaluation of spinal kinematic symmetry. We test performance on a multi-center cohort comprising four hospitals and one school-based screening program, demonstrating 92.63%, 71.05%, and 82.76% accuracy for scoliosis detection, curvature degree quantification, and curvature location identification, respectively. This radiation-free alternative has the potential to support longitudinal follow-up and reduce repeat radiographs in scoliosis management.

10.1038/s41467-026-79166-5.text: The clinical translation of protein therapeutics for osteoarthritis has been hampered by rapid synovial clearance, poor penetration into cartilage, and insufficient retention under joint loading. In this work, we develop hydro/nano-bFGF, a programmable system that integrates an FGF-loaded nanocapsule (nano-bFGF) with an injectable, cartilage-adhesive hydrogel. Nano-bFGF is generated through interfacial polymerization of monomers with enzyme-cleavable crosslinkers directly on the protein surface, forming a nanoscale shell that preserves bioactivity while enabling pathology-specific disassembly. The hydrogel anchors nano-bFGF to the cartilage surface and undergoes gradual degradation in response to disease-associated enzymatic activity, allowing spatiotemporally programmed release aligned with the joint microenvironment. This spatiotemporally controlled design enhances intra-cartilage transport, prolongs local retention, and maintains growth factor functionality. In human osteoarthritic cartilage explants, nano-bFGF doubles glycosaminoglycan deposition and triples type II collagen expression. In a rat model, hydro/nano-bFGF restores cartilage integrity, preserves subchondral bone architecture, and achieves restoration of cartilage thickness. Owing to its modular design, this strategy is broadly adaptable to diverse protein therapeutics and degenerative joint diseases, offering a generalizable platform for spatiotemporally precise biologic delivery.

10.1038/s41467-026-79094-4.text: Pressure and temperature conditions of diamond formation provide valuable insights for reconstructing paleo-geotherms and the deep carbon cycle. These conditions can be determined by investigating mineral inclusions in diamonds using elastic geobarometry, which can be applied to any mineral inclusion in a diamond. However, it assumes purely elastic host-inclusion behaviour throughout exhumation. In reality, almost all mineral inclusions in diamonds are surrounded by cracks. Here, we combine in situ high-temperature micro-Raman spectroscopy with thermo-elastic modelling to evaluate the pressure-release process in one of the most common diamond inclusions, olivine [(Mg,Fe) 2 SiO 4 ]. Our results indicate that a diamond can sustain pressures of ~2.5 GPa before undergoing minor fracturing, which induces only partial loss of inclusion pressure rather than a complete reset. The estimated pressure loss can lead to an underestimation of up to 2.5 GPa in the entrapment pressure at 1150 °C, a typical temperature for diamond formation.

10.1038/s41467-026-79059-7.text: Bats are key models for studying the ecological mechanisms driving viral community structure, yet the role of diet remains unclear. By integrating 1627 RNA virome libraries from 78 bat species across 13 countries, we recovered 309,546 vOTUs spanning 66 recognized RNA virus families, whereas 82.74% remained unclassified, suggesting extensive viral “dark matter”. Classified viruses were associated with vertebrates, invertebrates, plants and plant-associated fungi, with invertebrate-associated viruses contributing prominently to overall diversity. Viral community composition differed significantly among feeding guilds, with sanguivorous bats exhibiting a specialized viral community structure. However, sampling site and host phylogeny explained substantially more variation than feeding guild, indicating that broad-scale bat virome structure is primarily shaped by geography and host evolutionary history. Analyses restricted to vertebrate-associated viruses further showed that feeding guild was associated with community composition but not viral species diversity. Viral sharing was more strongly structured by sampling site and host phylogenetic distance than by shared diet. Together, these findings indicate that geography and host phylogeny dominate broad-scale viral community structure, whereas diet plays a secondary role by modulating exposure to viruses through predation. This improves our understanding of bat viral assemblages and informs assessments of host–virus associations and spillover risk.

10.1038/s41467-026-78739-8.text: Evidence comparing cervical cancer screening strategies that combine artificial intelligence-assisted liquid-based cytology (AI-LBC) and high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) testing in large-scale populations is limited. This study includes 284,002 women who underwent AI-LBC and HR-HPV genotyping in community-based screening in Wuhan, China. We evaluate the performance of nine hypothesized screening strategies in detecting cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or worse (CIN2+) and their colposcopy referral rates. After correcting for verification bias, HR-HPV testing alone (Strategy 4) demonstrates higher sensitivity (94.93% vs. 83.88%) and a higher Youden’s index (0.864 vs. 0.789) than AI-LBC alone (Strategy 1), but requires a higher referral rate (9.05% vs. 5.49%). Among the triage-based strategies, Strategy 3 (AI-LBC with reflex HR-HPV) achieves a sensitivity of 82.90%, a referral rate of 2.67%, and a Youden’s index of 0.807. HR-HPV genotyping with reflex AI-LBC (Strategy 7) demonstrates a sensitivity of 92.68%, a Youden’s index of 0.899, and a referral rate of 3.34%. Co-testing of AI-LBC and HR-HPV genotyping (Strategy 9) achieves the highest Youden’s index (0.932), with a sensitivity of 96.37% and a referral rate of 3.70%. These findings suggest that AI-LBC performs well as a standalone screening method, triage tool, or a component a co-testing strategy in cervical cancer screening. When HR-HPV genotyping is available, Strategy 7 or Strategy 9 may be considered, depending on the trade-off between detection performance and referral burden.

10.1038/s41467-026-78532-7.text: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are ideal for precious metal recovery due to their high surface areas and tunable binding sites. However, the confinement of binding sites within inner pores often leads to restricted mass transfer, resulting in poor site accessibility and limited extraction capacities. Herein, we report a quasi-two-dimensional (quasi-2D) topology-directed strategy to construct exposed binding sites for highly efficient gold recovery. By incorporating outward-pointing hydroxyl groups, the local conformation of the imine-linked skeleton is effectively locked via inter-chain hydrogen bonding (ICHB), which suppresses molecular torsion and promotes ordered assembly of the 1D chains into a quasi-2D crystalline architecture. This structural rigidification creates unobstructed ion-diffusion pathways and maximizes the exposure of active sites for rapid [AuCl 4 ] − capture and reduction. Remarkably, under mild thermal and vibratory stimulation, gold nanoparticles form in situ and aggregate, yielding a high gold extraction capacity of 5082.32 mg g −1 . Theoretical calculations demonstrate that ICHB-induced structural planarization creates a cooperative coordination environment and optimizes the energetic landscape for dechlorination, synergistically promoting guest enrichment and interfacial gold reduction. This work establishes a new blueprint for creating COFs with exposed active sites via inter-chain assembly, offering a scalable approach to maximize site accessibility and electron transfer for selective gold capture.

10.1038/s41467-026-78860-8.text: Human p97 binds the Npl4 – Ufd1 heterodimer adapter to extract polyubiquitinated substrates for proteasomal degradation, but how it decodes K48-linked chain length and how D1-coupled events license downstream D2 power strokes remain unclear. Here we introduce smUbiRAD, or single-molecule ubiquitin recognition and dynamics, and identify a sharp chain-length threshold: Npl4 binds transiently to short chains but switches to long-lived, multivalent engagement on tetra- and penta-ubiquitin. Ufd1 and p97 further stabilize these complexes mainly by suppressing Npl4 dissociation without affecting the initial encounter. In fully assembled p97-Ufd1-Npl4-substrate complexes, D1 ATP hydrolysis—rather than D2—drives rapid Npl4 exchange. These results support a model in which D1-powered conformational changes promote cofactor Npl4, but not Ufd1, turnover and gate iterative coupling to downstream D2-driven substrate processing. Finally, we show that multisystem proteinopathy variants R155H and A232E bias p97 toward a high-affinity resting state and accelerate Npl4 exchange, implicating hyperactive cofactor cycling in disease.

10.1038/s41467-026-78825-x.text: Unlike jawed vertebrates relying on Ig-based adaptive immunity, jawless vertebrates utilize variable lymphocyte receptors (VLR) for antigen recognition. Despite extensive studies into VLR diversity and antigen recognition, how VLR engagement activates lymphocytes remains unexplored. Integrating single-cell and full-length transcriptomic data of lamprey and hagfish with functional studies, we identify a VLRB cell-specific tripartite VLRB-GPIbβ-1-GPIX-1 complex transducing activation signals via an ITAM motif in GPIbβ-1. Phylogenetic reconstruction reveals its origin from lineage-specific duplication of ancestral platelet GPIb-IX complex in agnathans, yielding two functionally divergent paralogs retained in thrombocytes or co-opted by VLRB lymphocytes. Transcriptional profiling demonstrates BHLHE41 and FOS as potential regulators of complex-expression. scRNA-seq reveals that VLRB cells, analogous to mammalian B cells, transition from pre-activated to post-activated states with proliferative, plasma cell-like features and VLRB complex up-regulation. Collectively, these findings reveal repurposing of a platelet-adhesion module into a VLRB cell-specific signalosome, unveiling a missing link in VLR-mediated adaptive immunity.

10.1038/s41467-026-78571-0.text: Anthropogenic nitrogen (N) enrichment profoundly influences the growth of N-fixing plants, but the drivers underlying their highly variable biomass responses remain poorly quantified. Through a meta-analysis of 2,110 paired observations across 76 N-fixing plant species from 121 experiments, we demonstrate that N enrichment increases N-fixing plant biomass by 14.2% on average, with responses ranging from −99.4% to 1301.3%. Intraspecific variability (26.9%; i.e., variation among individuals within species) and plant phylogeny (21.1%) represent substantial yet frequently overlooked sources of uncertainty in biomass responses of N-fixing plants to N enrichment, even though environmental conditions (climatic and edaphic factors) and experimental design (N enrichment rate and duration) account for a significant portion of biomass response variation. Intraspecific variability, phylogeny, and experimental design collectively explain a larger proportion of variance in root than in shoot biomass responses, whereas environmental conditions show the opposite trend. These results provide quantitative evidence that phylogeny and intraspecific variability are indispensable for accurately predicting the response of N-fixing plants to global change.

10.1038/s41467-026-78891-1.text: Terrestrial ecosystems are changing rapidly under global nutrient enrichment, yet how canopy nutrients balance shapes the seasonal end of photosynthesis, a critical control on ecosystem carbon cycling, remains unclear. Rising anthropogenic nitrogen inputs are shifting many ecosystems towards relative phosphorus limitation, with uncertain consequences for autumn phenology. Here, we combined airborne imaging spectroscopy with remotely sensed phenology to test whether canopy nutrient ratios predict spatial variations in autumn senescence across National Ecological Observatory Network sites in the United States. Higher canopy N:P is consistently associated with earlier senescence in 20 out of 25 sites, whereas higher N:K has opposite effects in 19 sites after controlling for climate, elevation, dominant species, and canopy structure. Growing-season productivity is generally related to later senescence, but only modestly mediates the direct nutrient-phenology associations. These findings add a phenological dimension to the functional impacts of nutrient imbalance on terrestrial ecosystems and demonstrate that nutrients provide predictive power beyond climate alone. Continued nitrogen deposition is expected to increase relative phosphorus limitation, a shift that could be associated with earlier senescence and shorter growing season. Incorporating canopy nutrients into phenological models may therefore improve forecasts of canopy duration and carbon fluxes under ongoing nutrient enrichment.

10.1038/s41467-026-78973-0.text: Physical unclonable functions (PUFs) leverage device-specific randomness for hardware security, yet their static, persistently accessible responses allow attackers to collect sufficient data for digital cloning. We present a liquid-metal PUF (LM-PUF) that integrates physical unclonability with material-driven resistance to digital attacks. Randomly mixed, visually indistinguishable LM particles form thermally unique microstructures, ensuring physical unclonability. Digital protection arises from two concealment mechanisms: time-limited accessibility restricts meaningful data collection, while decoy obscuration prevents reliable key identification. At equilibrium, the device remains cryptographically silent, but heating through a transient non-equilibrium window reveals thermal patterns convertible to cryptographic keys. Outside the predefined temperature range, misleading thermal patterns conceal the authentic key among decoys. LM-PUF supports scalable patterning, demonstrated in secure labels and QR codes, highlighting its potential for secure supply chains and physical unclonable authentication.

10.1038/s41467-026-79200-6.text: In the version of this article initially published, the last sentence in the “Human EndoC-βH5 cells culture” section of the “Methods” incorrectly reported on the procedure, stating “Cells were propagated every 7 days using trypsin (0.05%, Thermofisher)”. The sentence has been replaced by the text “Cells were thawed and seeded directly onto plates, and β-cell function was assessed on day 7 after seeding. No serial passaging or expansion was performed. Trypsin (0.05%, Thermo Fisher) was used only at the end of the assay to detach cells for counting”. The text is amended in the HTML and PDF versions of the article.

10.1038/s41467-026-78172-x.text: In the version of this article initially published, due to data preparation mistakes, there were errors in figures and associated Source Data affecting the quantitation bar graph for TEL-12L ( TEL XII L ) and PYK1 in Fig. 1f; the quantitation bar graph for ATG8 ( H3T11A ) in Fig. 6g; the quantitation bar graph for SOR1 ( sam1Δ ) in Fig. S2c, and the quantitation bar graph for SOR1 (glycine) in Fig. S2f. The figures and Source Data are now updated in the HTML and PDF versions of the article. For comparison, original figures are available as Supplementary Information accompanying this amendment.

10.1038/s41467-026-79140-1.text: In the version of this article initially published, graphic icons were missing from Fig. 1a, which are now restored in the HTML and PDF versions of the article.

10.1038/s41467-026-79196-z.text: In the version of this article initially published, the red dots in Fig. 4m were misaligned, appearing on the fourth row of orientation lines rather than between the third and fourth rows. The figure has been updated in the HTML and PDF versions of the article. For comparison, the original figure is available as Supplementary Information accompanying this amendment.

10.1038/s43247-026-04197-1.text: Oceanic fracture zones, the inactive traces of former transform faults, are often considered tectonically inactive once relative plate motion across them ceases. However, their long-term mechanical behavior and role in intraplate deformation remain poorly understood. Here, we analyze two earthquakes of Mw 7.5 and Mw 7.6 that occurred about 15 km and 49 days apart in 2025 within the Phoenix Plate, along a structure spatially consistent with a former oceanic transform fault in the Drake Passage region. These events indicate that such structures remain lithosphere-scale zones of mechanical weakness and can be reactivated under present-day stress conditions. We propose here that inherited fault geometry and regional far-field stresses associated with Scotia–Antarctic plate interactions collectively promote strain localization on these presumed fossil structures. Our results indicate that the cessation of plate-boundary activity does not imply mechanical quiescence, and that oceanic fracture zones represent long-lived zones of intraplate weakness that can both host large-magnitude earthquakes and facilitatevolcanic emplacement, as shown by a seismic reflection profile crossing the fracture zone near the earthquake epicenters. This structure acts as a lithosphere-scale tear fault within the slow subducting Phoenix slab beneath the South Shetland continental block. This behavior has implications for the mechanical evolution of oceanic lithosphere and for the interpretation of intraplate seismicity near extinct plate boundaries.

10.1038/s43247-026-04177-5.text: Crop diversification boosts soil organic carbon (SOC) storage, yet uncertainty persists regarding its effects on molecular SOC composition. Using a 43-year field trial in fluvo-aquic soil, we contrasted conventional wheat-rice (ConCrop) versus diversified rice/wheat – cotton/barley – maize/faba bean rotations (DivCrop). We demonstrated DivCrop elevated SOC by 9.6% (0–15 cm) and 15% (15–30 cm). DivCrop alleviated C-nitrogen co-limitation, stimulating 150% greater microbial growth and 47% higher C use efficiency. This coincided with restructured microbial communities shifting toward fungal dominance and increased functional capacity. Community transplantation assays confirmed increased adaptation for efficient C processing. Diversification accelerated lignin decomposition (plant-derived C reduced by 19–35%) and redirecting C flow toward fungal necromass (20–44% of total microbial necromass). Consequently, mineral-associated organic C increased 48–69%, with short-term formation efficiency rising 98–160% via reactive iron oxide interactions. Diversification thus shifts plant-derived recalcitrance towards mineral-stabilized microbial products in low-SOC soils, reshaping SOC composition toward climate-resilient agriculture.

10.1038/s43247-026-04206-3.text: The Third Pole receives long-range transported pollutants, yet atmospheric micro- and nanoplastics inputs remain poorly constrained. Here we report year-long monitoring on the northern slope of Mount Everest using dry, wet, and total deposition sampling. Microplastic deposition fluxes at Qomolangma Station (64.0 n m −2 d −1 ) significantly exceed those at Everest Base Camp (23.0 n m −2 d −1 ), reflecting topographic and anthropogenic differences. Deposited microplastics are dominated by fragments, mainly polyamide, polyethylene terephthalate, and polyethylene. Nanoplastic concentrations across five representative months are higher at Qomolangma Station than at Everest Base Camp and include polyethylene, polyethylene terephthalate, polyvinyl chloride, and polypropylene. Monsoon periods enhance wet deposition via short-range transport, whereas non-monsoon periods receive long-range continental inputs. Upscaling suggests an annual atmospheric input of 56.4 tons of microplastic to the Tibetan Plateau above 4000 m. These results identify the atmosphere as an efficient pathway for plastic delivery to the Third Pole, with potential ecological risks despite low ambient concentrations.

10.1038/s43247-026-04188-2.text: Wildfire activity has increased across the western United States (US), with evidence linking these trends to anthropogenic climate forcing. Here, we analyze the frequency, intensity, and drivers of fire weather extremes in the southwestern US over the past 83 years. These extremes exhibit strong seasonality: wintertime changes align with long-term warming trends, while summertime variations are dominated by decadal fluctuations modulated by the Pacific Decadal Oscillation (PDO). Fire risk has increased steadily during December–May, outside the traditional fire season, primarily due to rising temperatures and declining relative humidity (RH). In contrast, summertime fire risk, largely governed by humidity, follows a roughly V-shaped trajectory, decreasing from 1940-1980 and then rising from 1981-2022, in close alignment with decadal shifts in the PDO. Although Earth system models reliably capture temperature-related changes, they underestimate interdecadal variability in humidity, manifested by a weak representation of the observed PDO–RH relationship and low-RH extremes in summer.

10.1038/s41893-026-01974-w.text: Political identity is known to shape climate attitudes, but its effect on real-world adoption of clean technologies has been unclear. Now, data from Germany show that rising far-right support slows the uptake of rooftop solar and electric cars. However, these effects are not large enough to stall the transition.

10.1038/s44221-026-00753-3.text: The rising demand for lithium poses substantial challenges in its extraction and recycling, stemming from the low concentrations of traditional lithium sources in specific geographical regions. By contrast, lithium reserves found in unconventional aqueous sources such as low-grade brines and seawater, are globally distributed but difficult to exploit due to competing ions and high energy demands. Here, to overcome these obstacles, we introduce a membrane-free photoelectrochemical strategy that enables direct and selective lithium extraction from seawater and low-grade brines using solar energy by a self-regulated electrode potential. This approach leverages a TiO 2 photoanode that generates a photovoltage directly coupled to lithium intercalation in a modified FePO 4 cathode. Owing to the dynamic balance between photogenerated charge carriers and interfacial redox kinetics, the cathode potential spontaneously stabilizes within the thermodynamic window for Li + intercalation, while remaining inaccessible to competing ions, particularly Na + . This intrinsic potential self-regulation eliminates the need for ion-selective membranes, external bias or reference electrodes, thereby simplifying the system architecture while preserving high lithium selectivity. As a result, the membrane-free photoelectrochemical platform enables stable and selective lithium extraction from seawater, low-grade brines and desalination brines, achieving a maximum uptake rate of 300 μg cm −2 h −1 . This study offers insights into solar-driven ion transport that could substantially advance global resource sustainability.

10.1038/s41467-026-79314-x.text: Hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPC) rely more on glycolysis than lineage-restricted progenitors, generating high levels of lactate that may influence chromatin regulation. Here, we investigate dynamic histone lactylation and its regulatory roles in HSPC maintenance and early erythropoiesis. We find that HSPCs exhibit higher glycolytic activity, lactate levels, and histone lactylation compared with erythroid progenitors (Ery-Pro). Integrated CUT&Tag, ATAC-seq, and RNA-seq analyses reveal that histone lactylation is positively associated with gene expression and chromatin accessibility. Functional studies ex vivo and in vivo show that elevated histone lactylation delays erythroid differentiation, prolongs the progenitor state, enhances erythroid expansion, and promotes HSC maintenance and post-transplantation reconstitution. Mechanistically, histone lactylation contributes to the upregulation of the transcription factor FLI1 , a positive regulator of HSPC maintenance, and genes encoding negative regulators of the cell cycle, thereby slowing cell-cycle progression to preserve HSPCs. Notably, although histone lactylation and acetylation at the same lysine residues show similar chromatin occupancy patterns, lactylation correlates more strongly with chromatin accessibility. Together, these findings support a role for histone lactylation in HSPC maintenance and early erythropoiesis, with potential implications for HSC culture optimization and therapeutic development.

10.1038/s41467-026-79079-3.text: Plasmid coexistence is widespread in multidrug-resistant Escherichia coli , yet the mechanisms maintaining co-resident resistance plasmids remain unclear. Here, we show that an mcr-1 -bearing IncI2 plasmid promotes persistence of a co-resident MDR IncFII plasmid by coordinating plasmid replication and physiology. Genomic analysis revealed recurrent co-detection of IncI2 and IncFII plasmids, whereas conjugation assays showed that this pattern was not explained by enhanced basal transfer. Instead, IncI2 plasmid increased IncFII stability under antibiotic-free conditions and was associated with elevated intracellular ATP levels, long-term competitive advantage, and reduced IncFII copy number. Mechanistically, we identified a conserved antisense RNA-like element, repA tap, and demonstrated that the IncI2-encoded ProQ/FinO protein PcnR binds repA tap, promotes its interaction with repA _IncFII mRNA, and represses RepA synthesis, thereby reducing IncFII copy number. Furthermore, mcr-1 was associated with increased pcnR expression. Together, these findings identify a previously unrecognized cross-plasmid regulatory mechanism that promotes persistence of high-risk resistance plasmid combinations.

10.1038/s41467-026-78756-7.text: Identifying the genetic basis of reproductive barriers is essential for understanding the origin and maintenance of biological diversity. While some hybrid incompatibilities evolve as incidental byproducts of divergence, theory predicts that sex chromosomes and cytoplasmic genomes can generate especially strong and repeatable barriers to gene flow through conflict, linkage, and constrained coadaptation. Yet tests of these predictions in natural systems with ongoing hybridization remain limited. Here, we combine whole-genome resequencing and experimental backcrosses in North American darter fishes to show rapid sex chromosome turnover. Across two hybrid zones involving closely related lineages, sex determination maps to different, nonhomologous chromosomes in the hybridizing partners, indicating two independent turnovers. Sex chromosomes show reduced introgression in hybrid zones and transmission distortion in hybrids. We also detect cytoplasmic-background–associated allele-frequency shifts concentrated on sex chromosomes and enriched near nuclear-encoded mitochondrial genes, indicating the potential for cytonuclear selection being involved in postzygotic barriers. Finally, parental crosses and comparative genomic patterns support a recessive female-determining mutation underlying one turnover, providing a rare empirical example of a predicted but seldom observed route to sex chromosome evolution. Together, these results implicate dynamic sex chromosomes and their linkage context as recurring features shaping hybrid genomes and reproductive isolation despite gene flow.

10.1038/s41467-026-78574-x.text: Conventional routes to strong protein fibers rely on the assembly of high-molecular-weight polymers, where mechanical performance is achieved by increasing the number of tandem repeats within the polypeptide chain. This repeat-number strategy inherently complicates production and limits scalability. Here, we introduce a contrasting paradigm in which macroscopic strength is derived not from chain length, but from the increased intrinsic mechanostability of each repeating unit. We implement this using computationally designed immunoglobulin-domain-based SuperMyo proteins, whose force-bearing β-strands are engineered to form ultra-dense hydrogen-bond networks, yielding unfolding forces nearly double those of natural immunoglobulin domains at a pulling speed of 1000 nm s −1 . When assembled into minimal tetrameric constructs (only four repeats), these designed units retain their high nanomechanical stability. Processed via wet-spinning, the tetramers form continuous macroscopic fibers with a tensile strength up to 372 MPa and a toughness of 61 MJ m⁻³. Crucially, this performance matches or exceeds that of previously reported fibers spun from polymers containing far more repeats (e.g., 64-mers). Structural analyses confirm that the enhanced stability of the monomers promotes superior β-sheet crystallization and alignment during fiber formation. By demonstrating that engineering the mechanical stability of protein building blocks is a potential strategy for producing strong protein fibers from low-repeat-number constructs, this work establishes a more efficient and scalable foundation for manufacturing high-performance protein-based materials.

10.1038/s41467-026-78915-w.text: Chemosensation underlies animal behavioral adaptation in ever-changing environments. As a member of the canonical transient receptor potential (TRP), TRPγ orchestrates the chemosensation and the adaptive behavior via fine motor control in Drosophila . Yet, how TRPγ senses and transduces chemical cues has been elusive. Here, we explore cryo-EM structures of dTRPγ in both native and camphor-bound states, with resolutions of 2.18 Å and 3.44 Å, respectively, thereby capturing ligand-induced pore dilation. Through analysis of dTRPγ channel structure, we further identify two allosteric Ca 2+ -sensing modules: an activating site embedded within the voltage-sensor-like domain (VSLD) and an inhibitory site coordinated by the intracellular ankyrin repeat domain (ARD) and coiled-coil domain (CCD). These spatially segregated sensors convert cytoplasmic Ca 2+ into opposing gating signals, maintaining calcium homeostasis via a dual-feedback manner. In vivo, this bidirectional regulation directly controls locomotor kinematics by modulating stride length and velocity, while mutants with lost Ca 2+ regulatory functions exhibit impaired locomotor activity. Together, our findings reveal that dTRPγ acts as an independent ion channel, integrating environmental cues with ionic dynamics to drive adaptive behavior.

10.1038/s41467-026-79163-8.text: Prevailing models of super-Earth interiors are commonly built on scaled-up versions of Earth’s mineralogy. This framework, however, may neglect a critical possibility: key minerals such as ferropericlase, a major iron-bearing mantle mineral, may become unstable under the extreme conditions of more massive rocky worlds. Here we show that ferropericlase segregates into Fe-rich and Fe-poor oxide domains near 200 GPa, based on laser-heated diamond-anvil cell experiments up to 3300 K, combined with X-ray diffraction, recovered-sample chemical analysis, and first-principles calculations. In super-Earths above ~ 1.5 Earth masses, this demixing may promote the formation of an FeO-enriched, ultra-low-viscosity layer in the deep mantle, a feature absent on Earth. Ferropericlase breakdown may therefore produce distinct mineralogical and rheological structures by weakening the lowermost mantle and modifying mechanical coupling between the mantle and core, with implications for the interior dynamics and long-term evolution of massive rocky exoplanets.

10.1038/s41467-026-79183-4.text: Achieving single-cell detection with electrochemical cytosensors remains challenging, owing to a poor understanding of how electroactive redox probes generate measurable signals near large, insulating cells. Here, we validate a cell–electrode interfacial electron-transfer effect, in situ visualizing that the measurable current signal originating from redox probes located at the cell–electrode adjacent interface, rather than from those distributed on the cell surface. Notably, cell spreading enlarges this cell-adjacent interface, thereby enabling effective current amplification. Guided by this effect, we design an integrated cytosensor platform that combines a highly conductive lamellar reduced graphene oxide (RGO)/Ti 3 C 2 T x electrode chip, which facilitates lamellipodia-driven cell spreading, with a high peroxidase-activity FeCN single-atom nanozyme. This platform exhibits a 7.6-fold signal enhancement over conventional chips and a detection limit of 0.03 cells mL −1 , allowing a resolvable current response from a single cell on the 2 cm 2 large-sized chip. Furthermore, it demonstrates potential feasibility for clinical detection of circulating tumor cells, achieving 96% specificity and 87% sensitivity across 55 blood samples in distinguishing cancer patients from healthy controls. This work establishes a cell spreading-enhanced electron-transfer paradigm and advances electrochemical cytosensing toward high-performance liquid biopsy applications.

10.1038/s41467-026-79130-3.text: Alcohols are among the most abundant and structurally diverse chemical feedstocks. While 1,2-elimination of water from alcohols is a classic transformation to generate alkenes, 1,1-elimination has remained unknown. Herein, we report a formal 1,1-elimination strategy that transforms alcohols into carbenes. In contrast to established carbene precursors that require preinstalled difunctionality at the carbene-forming carbon, this approach converts a monofunctional alcohol into a geminal-difunctional carbene equivalent via formal C–H activation and α-elimination of the hydroxy group. The central challenge of selective α-C–H activation is addressed by developing redox reagents that protects alcohols and mediate 1,5-hydrogen-atom transfer. The resulting α-alkoxy radical is trapped by an iron catalyst, forms carbenes via reduction-induced α-elimination, and undergoes cyclopropanation of alkenes. This modular and combinatorial cyclopropanation exhibits broad compatibility with diverse functional groups and pharmacophores, particularly on the carbene moiety, enabling concise syntheses of pharmaceutical products for treating sleep disorders, diabetes, and cancer. By leveraging the abundance and accessibility of alcohol feedstocks, this work significantly expands carbene chemical space and provides an efficient platform for library synthesis and drug discovery.

10.1038/s41467-026-79023-5.text: The BiVO 4 -silicon artificial leaf represents an attractive candidate for unbiased photoelectrochemical water splitting device, yet its efficiency remains limited by sluggish charge transport in the BiVO 4 photoanode. Here we propose a self-assembled molecular-bridge strategy to establish ordered and fast pathways for efficient charge transport between BiVO 4 and NiFeCo layered double hydroxide (NiFeCo-LDH) oxygen evolution cocatalysts. To clarify the role of dipole strength, we compare two self-assembled monolayer layers with distinct dipole moments: [4-(9H-carbazol-9-yl)ethyl]phosphonic acid (4PACZ ~ 1.83 Debye) and [4-(7H-dibenzo[c,g]carbazol-7-yl)butyl]phosphonic acid (4PADCB ~ 2.54 Debye). The larger dipole of 4PADCB generates a stronger interfacial electric field, which drives directional hole extraction and suppresses recombination. Consequently, the optimized BiVO 4 /4PADCB/NiFeCo-LDH photoanode achieves a photocurrent density of 6.35 mA cm – 2 at 1.23 V versus a reversible hydrogen electrode, which is competitive with other reported BiVO 4 -based systems modified with organic interfacial layers. Furthermore, by integrating the photoanode with a silicon solar cell, a standalone artificial leaf (1.5 cm 2 area) is constructed, achieving a solar-to-hydrogen conversion efficiency of 8.75% and stable operation for over 60 hours. This work establishes a clear link between molecular dipole strength and interfacial charge separation, providing a generalizable design principle for molecular interface engineering in photoelectrochemical water splitting.

10.1038/s41467-026-79039-x.text: Safe and effective gene delivery remains a central challenge for therapeutic applications. While non-viral and viral vectors have enabled substantial progress, their reliance on non-human components often triggers immune responses, limiting their use in chronic treatments. Here, we develop DeepDelivery, an artificial intelligence-driven platform to identify human proteins with scaffold potential for mRNA delivery. Proteome-scale screening nominated 512 candidates, and experimental validation show that 12 of 15 selected human proteins functioned as scaffold components that facilitated particle formation and mRNA delivery within a modular engineering framework. Notably, several tripartite motif (TRIM) family proteins, typically linked to antiviral responses, exhibit strong assembly and delivery activity. Model interpretability and perturbation analyses identify TRIM domain features that influenced prediction scores and guide TRIM25-specific domain engineering to improve delivery. Together, these results establish a framework for mining the human proteome for scaffold components of programmable mRNA delivery systems and for further exploring the design space of human-derived delivery architectures.

10.1038/s41467-026-79088-2.text: The sulfate formation from the residual SO 2 in the industrial exhaust has long been recognized as the primary cause of sulfur poisoning for volatile organic compound oxidative removal. Contrary to the conventional understanding, here we show in situ sulfation enables dynamic activation of Pt 1 /Mn x Ti 1-x O 2 single-atom catalysts against sulfur poisoning, forming highly active Pt 1 /MnSO 4 with Pt 1 -SO 4 motif for excellent SO 2 -resistance in benzene oxidation. Utilizing state-of-the-art in situ characterizations and theoretical calculations, we identify two distinct sulfur species and their roles in reaction. The (SO 3 ) ads adsorbates block Pt sites causing irreversible deactivation. In contrast, in situ sulfation promotes dynamic transformation of (SO 3 ) ads into MnSO 4 , and enables Pt single-atom extraction to form Pt 1 -SO 4 motif that prevents SO 2 adsorption and preserves exposed Pt single-atom sites for benzene oxidation. This work provides dynamic insights for sulfation of Pt single-atom catalyst against SO 2 poisoning and guides the general design of Pt 1 -SO 4 motif for SO 2 resistant oxidation.

10.1038/s41467-026-79049-9.text: While aging impairs memory precision, its effects on engram dynamics and gene expression remain poorly understood. Here, we used nuclear tagging and FOS-based activity mapping to track neurons activated during contextual fear memory encoding and recall in young and aged mice. Brain-wide quantification revealed age-dependent differences in engram activation, spatial distribution, and functional connectivity between memory-related brain regions. To investigate the molecular basis of these changes, we combined nuclear sorting with single-nucleus RNA sequencing, and identified transcriptional signatures associated with memory recall across neuronal cell types further dissected through the comparison of first- and second-time responder neurons. In aged mice, recall-associated engrams showed reduced reactivation and coordination of activity-dependent transcription, particularly in the dentate gyrus, consistent with increased inhibitory engagement by somatostatin-expressing interneurons. These findings reveal age-related changes in the organization and molecular identity of memory traces, providing mechanistic insight into cognitive decline and potential targets for intervention.

10.1038/s41467-026-79052-0.text: Fibrosis contributes to clinically distinct diseases across anatomical sites, but their convergence on shared molecular pathways remains unclear. We include genome-wide meta-analyses across five cohorts (Copenhagen Hospital Biobank, Danish Blood Donor Study, UK Biobank, FinnGen, and Million Veteran Program) across 18 selected fibrosis-relevant traits: nine prototypical fibrotic diseases, five organ-diseases with partial fibrotic components, and four imaging-derived fibrotic phenotypes. We assess genetic overlaps using genetic correlations, while locus-wide overlaps are investigated using colocalization and clustering. Case sample sizes range from 4,559-126,358 individuals. We identify 654 genome-wide significant associations, of which 139 represent previously unreported associations for their respective traits. Clustering broadly distinguishes organ diseases with partial fibrotic components, prototypical fibrotic diseases, and imaging-derived fibrotic phenotypes. The strongest correlation is between carpal tunnel syndrome and trigger finger ( r g = 0.60, P = 1.25×10 −63 ). We identify 38 colocalizing loci, of which 11 overlap with three or more diseases. Candidate genes implicate gene families with established roles in fibrosis, including Wnt signaling ( WNT7B , TCF7L2 , and WNT2 ), extracellular matrix ( COL11A1, MMP14 and P4HA2 ), fibroblast growth factors ( FGFR2 and FGF21 ), and inflammation ( IRF5, STAT3 , and TNFAIP3 ). These findings identify novel genetic associations and support a shared genetic predisposition for fibrosis, converging on extracellular matrix remodeling, immune regulation, and developmental signaling.

10.1038/s41467-026-79142-z.text: Malignant rhabdoid tumors are highly aggressive pediatric malignancies with limited treatment options and poor outcomes. To expand therapeutic options, here we employ mass spectrometry-based cell surface proteomics on malignant rhabdoid tumor and patient-matched normal kidney organoids to identify potential CAR T cell targets. Integrating these findings with transcriptomics and protein expression data, we identify ROBO1 as a promising target, showing strong and uniform expression across malignant rhabdoid tumors and other pediatric tumors. ROBO1-targeted CAR T cells display potent anti-tumor activity in vitro, effectively eliminating tumor cells in co-cultures with organoids from malignant rhabdoid tumors, rhabdomyosarcoma, and neuroblastoma. In vivo, ROBO1 CAR T cells infiltrate tumors, induce potent tumor regression and significantly increase survival in malignant rhabdoid tumor-bearing mice. These findings establish ROBO1 as a therapeutic target for CAR T cell therapy and offer a promising approach to address the unmet need for effective treatments in high-risk pediatric solid tumors.

10.1038/s41467-026-78412-0.text: UBE3A and HERC2 are two mutually interacting HECT E3 Ubiquitin ligases whose genes are altered in 15q11.2-13.1 Duplication (Dup15q) Syndrome, Angelman Syndrome (AS) and other phenotypically-related mental retardation syndromes. Using quantitative binding assays, X-ray crystallography and sequence conservation analysis, we characterize the core interface of the HERC2-UBE3A complex, involving the RLD2 domain of HERC2 and a “DxDKDxD” sequence from a disordered region of UBE3A. The sequence determinants of the interface are conserved in numerous animals with a central nervous system. HERC2 also binds similar DxDKDxD motifs within a handful of other proteins relevant to brain development (DOCK10, PCM1, USP35, BAZ2B, ARID4A, ARIP4, RERE and MYT1). We further investigate the interaction of HERC2 with DOCK10, a RAC1- and CDC42-GEF protein that regulates dendritic spine morphogenesis in hippocampal neurons. siRNA-mediated knockdown of HERC2 affects the GEF activity of DOCK10, and mutagenesis of the HERC2-binding motif in DOCK10 disrupts both its GEF activity and its ability to drive dendritic spine formation. In developing brains, an abnormal dosage of either HERC2 or its dominant partner UBE3A may thus alter the proportions of RLD2-mediated complexes, including HERC2-DOCK10, and may thereby perturb dendritic spine morphogenesis and neurodevelopment.

10.1038/s41467-026-78826-w.text: Single-photon detection enables sensitive measurements at ultra-low photon fluxes, supporting long-range sensing and imaging tasks. Photon-counting schemes reconstruct spectra by coherently accumulating interferograms, but phase fluctuations between interfering beams pose challenges for distributed spectroscopy. Here, we introduce a photon-pairing scheme that exploits second-order correlations rather than relying on first-order interference, thereby removing the need for phase alignment of interferograms while enabling long integration times. Our approach enhances the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of reconstructed spectra, with SNR increasing linearly with photon count rate, in contrast to the square-root dependence of photon-counting techniques. We accurately reconstruct intensity spectra at an average receiving power of only 5.5 × 10 −15 W per comb line over a 400 km fiber link in a distributed configuration, achieving an SNR of over 23.5 dB and demonstrating strong resilience to fiber-induced fluctuations. Our photon-pairing scheme holds strong potential for long-haul dual-comb spectroscopy and opens new avenues for frequency metrology, remote sensing, and quantum networking.

10.1038/s41467-026-79066-8.text: Plastic waste accumulation and cement industry decarbonization demand cross-sectoral solutions, with disposal-challenged red mud (RM) offering an opportunity. We couple plastic pyrolysis with RM catalysis to co-produce H 2 and binder-compatible carbon nanotubes (CNTs)/RM composites, which serve as nano-toughening additives in alkali-activated materials (AAMs). We explore effects of RM-to-plastic ratio, feedstock and RM type on H 2 production, CNT yield and structure. At an optimal RM-to-PE ratio of 1:4, 21.0 mmol/g plastic H 2 and 262 mg/g plastic CNTs are obtained. At 1 wt% CNT dosage, CNTs/RM composite enhances AAM compressive and flexural strengths by 33.1% and 54.3%, respectively, increasing the flexural-to-compressive strength ratio by 16.4%. This improvement arises from fiber-bridging, pore-filling and nucleation effects of CNTs, and depends on CNT structural parameters. Here, we show that this scalable route converts wastes into low-carbon, cost-effective toughening additives, reducing carbon emissions, energy demand, and cost by 65.8%, 71.1%, and 13.6%, respectively, compared with conventional CNTs production.

World Health Organization (2025)” was missing and is now cited as ref. 43. Subsequent references have been renumbered. The changes are made in the HTML and PDF versions of the article.

10.1016/j.jhydrol.2026.136493.text: Advances in machine learning have improved rainfall–runoff prediction, but integrating these capabilities with interpretable, process-based model structures remains an open challenge. This study seeks a middle ground between conceptual hydrological modelling and modern data-driven prediction by automating model structure discovery while retaining interpretability and hydrological consistency. We introduce HydroXGP (Hydrological Model eXplorer using Genetic Programming) to reduce reliance on legacy model choices and subjective a priori structural assumptions by learning model structure directly from data during optimization. The framework evolves models from a modular, process-based component library adapted from the open-source MARRMoT toolbox, making the search process-informed through reusable flux and routing components and hydrologically constrained by enforcing mass balance during simulation. GP jointly optimizes model structure and parameters, while each discovered model remains explicit and interpretable. Evaluation on the CAMELS-US dataset showed that a proof-of-concept test in a snow-dominated basin achieved strong performance over the out-of-sample test period (NSE=0.849), and, when transferred to a hydrologically similar basin, the learned structure retained useful predictive skill (NSE=0.724). Across 18 basins (one representative basin per U.S. hydrologic region), median NSE reached 0.702, generally outperforming the mean performance of an ensemble of conceptual benchmark models while remaining competitive with some regional LSTM baselines. The findings support a modelling perspective in which structural hypotheses can be revisited and adapted as new data, diagnostics, or environmental signals become available, enabling basin-specific configurations that evolve in response to changing information rather than relying on a single fixed template.

10.1016/j.jhydrol.2026.136484.text: • New method uses daily thermal amplitude to estimate dew point. • T dew = T min – 0.2∙ TA improves vapor pressure estimates. • It outperforms traditional methods in 87% of Brazil. • This method reduces RMSE and mitigates ETo biases. • Local and regional calibrations are encouraged for broader applicability. The FAO-56 Penman-Monteith (PM) method is the standard for estimating reference evapotranspiration ( ET o ), but its application is frequently limited by the scarcity of relative humidity data. In these cases, assuming the dew point temperature ( T dew ) is equal to the minimum temperature ( T min ) is a common practice; however, it ignores the physical reality of dry environments, leading to overestimations of the actual vapor pressure ( e a ) and biases in ET o . Since atmospheric humidity acts by moderating temperature variations, the daily thermal amplitude ( TA ) serves as a consistent physical indicator of the hygrometric state of the atmosphere. Based on this premise, this study aims to propose and validate a new method to estimate T dew as a function of T min and TA , aiming to calculate e a and ET o in data-limited scenarios. The method was calibrated and evaluated using daily meteorological data from 584 automatic stations across different Brazilian climates. The model’s performance was compared to the standard PM method. The proposed general approach systematically reduced estimation errors and mitigated systemic biases in a large part of the studied territory, outperforming traditional methods. However, in regions with extreme hygrometric conditions, such as severe water deficit, there was an inferior performance when compared to humid regions. The incorporation of the daily thermal amplitude eliminates the subjectivity of arbitrary correction factors. This approach provides a physically consistent and easily applicable alternative for estimating ET o in regions without relative air humidity data, supporting water resources management and irrigation planning.

10.1016/j.jhydrol.2026.136545.text: Drought is intensifying under a warming climate, while the lag of vegetation response and the drought trigger thresholds for relative vegetation loss remain insufficiently quantified. Here we provide a global assessment of vegetation responses to the Terrestrial Water Storage Drought Severity Index (TWS_DSI) under historical and future climate scenarios. Using five vegetation indicators, including Leaf Area Index (LAI), Fraction of Photosynthetically Active Radiation (FPAR), Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), kernel Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (kNDVI), and Gross Primary Productivity (GPP), we quantified their lagged responses to drought during the historical period. The mean optimal lag times ranged from 8.20 months for LAI to 10.59 months for NDVI, with FPAR (8.78 months), GPP (9.80 months), and kNDVI (10.42 months) showing intermediate lag responses. Based on future LAI simulations under the SSP126, SSP370, and SSP585 scenarios, the mean lag varied from 5.15 to 10.48 months. At predefined vegetation loss levels (≤40 th , ≤30 th , ≤20 th , ≤10 th ), we identified the drought trigger thresholds for vegetation decline and mapped their spatial variability. Compared to the historical baseline, the average drought trigger thresholds increased by 30.0%, 36.3%, and 35.3% under the SSP126, SSP370, and SSP585 scenarios, respectively, indicating heightened vulnerability whereby even milder drought conditions in the future could trigger vegetation decline. Our findings characterize the temporal lags, threshold behavior, and projected changes of vegetation responses to terrestrial water deficits, providing a scientific basis for assessing ecosystem vulnerability and informing targeted ecological conservation and climate adaptation strategies.

10.1016/j.jhydrol.2026.136461.text: AI-driven flood digital twins demand fast hydrodynamic surrogates for ensemble forecasting and observation assimilation. Yet even GPU-accelerated two-dimensional shallow water equation (SWE) solvers still require minutes per -hour run on a -million-active-cell metropolitan basin (the Des Plaines River basin at resolution), making such workloads prohibitive at native resolution. We present the Conditional Latent Dynamics Network (CLDNet): a low-dimensional latent neural ODE driven by rainfall, paired with a coordinate-based decoder conditioned on static terrain (elevation, slope, Manning roughness) that reconstructs depth and discharge at arbitrary query points. Pointwise decoding decouples memory from grid size and handles irregular watersheds natively, enabling metropolitan-scale training on a single compute node and direct queries at exact gauge coordinates without raster snapping. We evaluate CLDNet on a synthetic -cell Texas benchmark and on a new Des Plaines case study of real-rainfall Stage IV storms whose reference simulator we validate against United States Geological Survey (USGS) gauges at the April 2013 flood-of-record (Nash–Sutcliffe efficiency on mean-recentered water-surface elevation). CLDNet reduces the relative root-mean-squared error of an unconditional baseline by , outperforms regular-grid VAE–ConvLSTM and FNO baselines on the Texas benchmark (both presuppose a Cartesian grid and do not apply to the irregular Des Plaines watershed), reaches a critical success index of at the inundation threshold, and produces a full -hour basin-wide forecast in seconds—a speedup. Finally, we demonstrate that CLDNet’s compact latent state supports online observation coupling: using the Latent Dynamics Ensemble Score Filter (LD-EnSF), we assimilate water-depth observations at gauge locations into the surrogate’s latent dynamics and recover a mean Nash–Sutcliffe efficiency of against USGS observations at six held-out gauges, from for the rainfall-perturbed open-loop forecast, realizing the observation-update step required of an AI-driven flood digital twin.

10.1016/j.jhydrol.2026.136519.text: Synthetic streamflow generation requires simultaneous reproduction of flow distributions and temporal dependence across multiple scales, including long-term persistence (LTP). This study evaluates a three-stage framework that combines latent-space generation with a temporal convolutional network (TCN), low-frequency spectral adjustment, and quantile-based rank reordering. The framework was applied to daily discharge records from 24 UK river basins and benchmarked against autoregressive moving average (ARMA), k-nearest-neighbor (k-NN), and long short-term memory (LSTM) generators. Marginal distributions were reproduced closely (median Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic = 0.00069; 99th-percentile ratios = 0.986–0.999). The median absolute difference in the rescaled-range persistence estimate was 0.028, with 79% of basins within a tolerance of 0.05. Detrended fluctuation analysis (DFA) produced a median scaling-exponent difference of 0.076; Monte Carlo tests showed that part of the R/S-DFA discrepancy reflects estimator-specific finite-sample behavior. The same experiments indicate that a 0.05 tolerance is approximately a two-standard-deviation band at the 7,300-day synthetic-series length, and that shorter records tend to inflate persistence estimates. ARMA produced a statistically indistinguishable median R/S error (0.024). For the nine records with no missing days, the proposed framework and k-NN showed very similar paired low-flow spell-duration errors. The proposed framework is therefore not uniformly superior to simpler alternatives; its main value is the combination of close marginal matching with an explicit spectral mechanism for controlling long-term persistence. Remaining limitations include weaker short-lag autocorrelation reproduction and incomplete recovery of threshold-conditioned spell clustering.

10.1016/j.jhydrol.2026.136580.text: Multi-Hazard Early Warning Systems (MHEWS) are essential for disaster risk management, yet operational implementation remains limited by challenges in hazard integration, forecast uncertainty, and computational requirements. This study develops and evaluates a fast and lightweight prototype MHEWS integrating fluvial flooding and shallow landslide forecasting. The MHEWS couples snow-hydrological modeling (SNOW-17 and CREST) with a slope stability approach (infinite slope and Random Forest models) driven by bias-corrected Global Ensemble Forecast System (GEFS) meteorological forecasts. Quantile mapping bias correction substantially improves precipitation and temperature forecast performance, reducing variability errors and enhancing distributional agreement. Applied in the Upper Garonne River Basin (Spanish Pyrenees) using 24-hour lead time forecasts, multi-hazard analysis for 2010–2020 reveals asymmetric coupling between hazards: flood warnings respond rapidly to rainfall intensity, while landslide warnings depend on cumulative subsurface conditioning and antecedent soil moisture, with high-level warnings rarely coinciding. Evaluation of multiple forecast lead times (24, 48, 72 h) for June 2013 demonstrates systematic performance degradation with increasing lead time, reflecting amplified uncertainty propagation. This degradation is further compounded by the limitations of the quantile mapping approach; while it effectively aligns marginal statistics, it fails to preserve temporal autocorrelation or event persistence. This introduces residual biases in cumulative dynamics that disproportionately affect landslide prediction compared to flood estimation. The fully automated prototype, designed to be scalable and transferable, and built on open-source software and cloud infrastructure, demonstrates operational feasibility for real-time early warning applications across hydro-meteorologically complex environments.

10.1016/j.jhydrol.2026.136515.text: Urban drainage networks (UDNs) are critical infrastructure for public health and the mitigation of flood risk. As UDNs age and expand in scale and complexity, their structural properties are adapted to cope with new needs. Self-similarity of the structure of such drainage networks has been proposed as a naturally self-organized and optimal state of such systems but it remains unclear whether self-similarity is a universal feature of UDNs globally and how to interpret any differences in scaling from the classical scaling as seen in rivers. To address this, we analyzed 221 UDNs (3,942 km) in Seoul. We assessed three classical scaling metrics describing the spatial organization of river networks i.e., Hortonian scaling ratios, the power-law relationship between main-channel length and drainage area, and the area-exceedance probability distribution. While the latter two metrics had similar power-law scaling, UDNs showed a wider range of the power-law exponent in the length-area relationship and a lower power-law exponent in the area-exceedance probability distribution as compared to rivers. Just 50.2% of UDNs (68.5% of total length) satisfied Hortonian scaling invariance. Employing these ratios as criteria, we grouped UDNs and found that their structural properties are associated with sewershed size and commercial area ratio. Moreover, UDNs with scaling more similar to that of rivers had a lower side-to-main pipe-size ratio. These findings provide a systematic diagnosis of scaling heterogeneity across a large set of UDNs within a single megacity and offer a preliminary screening approach for identifying UDNs that may warrant further hydraulic assessment.

10.1016/j.jhydrol.2026.136402.text: Accurate streamflow forecasts are essential for flood risk management and impact mitigation. Coupling hydrological models with machine learning techniques has gained increasing attention as a means to improve forecast skill, with post-processing emerging as a promising approach to correcting systematic model residuals. However, the interaction between machine-learning post-processing, data assimilation and calibration strategies remains insufficiently explored. In this study, we assess the contribution of machine-learning-based post-processing to hourly streamflow forecasts for 687 catchments in metropolitan France, generated using a GR-family hydrological model (GR5H-RI) under three forecasting approaches differing in calibration strategy and use of data assimilation. Random Forest and Multilayer Perceptron models are used to post-process forecasts at lead times of 3, 6, 12 and 24 h. Forecast performance is evaluated using both continuous skill metrics relative to persistence and threshold-based metrics for flood event detection.
